title: SASSA Disability Grant 2026: Eligibility, Medical Requirements & Application
description: Step-by-step guide to the SASSA Disability Grant (R2,400/month). Who qualifies, how the medical assessment works, required documents, payment dates, and how to appeal a denial.
author: Zanele Nkosi

sections.title: What is the SASSA Disability Grant?
sections.content: The SASSA Disability Grant is a monthly payment for South African citizens and permanent residents aged 18 to 59 who have a physical or mental disability that makes them unable to work for more than six months. As of 2026, the grant amount is {{disability_grant_amount}} per month. The grant is means-tested, meaning your income and assets must be below a certain threshold. A medical assessment by a state doctor is required to confirm the disability. The grant may be awarded temporarily (6 to 12 months) or permanently, depending on the nature of the disability.

sections.title: Eligibility Requirements
sections.content:
To qualify for the SASSA Disability Grant in 2026, you must meet all the following requirements:
  • Age: You must be between 18 and 59 years old.
  • Disability: You must have a physical or mental disability that prevents you from working for at least six months.
  • Medical assessment: A state doctor must confirm your disability. Private doctor reports may be considered but a state assessment is usually required.
  • Income threshold: Your income must not exceed {{disability_income_threshold_single}} per month if single, or {{disability_income_threshold_married}} combined if married.
  • Asset threshold: Your assets must not exceed {{disability_asset_threshold_single}} for a single person or {{disability_asset_threshold_married}} for a married couple.
  • Citizenship: You must be a South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee.

sections.title: Types of Disabilities That May Qualify
sections.content:
The Disability Grant covers a wide range of conditions, including but not limited to:
  • Physical disabilities affecting mobility (paralysis, amputation, severe arthritis)
  • Blindness or severe visual impairment
  • Deafness or severe hearing impairment
  • Mental health conditions (severe depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder)
  • Intellectual disabilities
  • Chronic medical conditions (HIV/AIDS with complications, tuberculosis, cancer, kidney disease)
  • Stroke or brain injury recovery
The condition must be confirmed by a medical professional and must substantially limit your ability to work.

sections.title: Required Documents
sections.content:
You need the following to apply for the Disability Grant:
  • 13-digit ID (green ID book or smart ID card)
  • Medical report from a doctor detailing your disability (form available at SASSA offices)
  • Proof of income — last 3 months bank statements, payslips, or affidavit
  • Proof of residence — utility bill or affidavit
  • Proof of assets — property valuations, investment statements if applicable
  • Medical records — hospital discharge summaries, specialist reports, test results

steps.title: Get a Medical Report
steps.content: Visit a doctor or clinic to obtain a medical report. SASSA provides a specific form (the MED 1 form) that your doctor must complete.

steps.title: Visit Your Nearest SASSA Office
steps.content: Take all your documents, including the medical report, to your nearest SASSA office.

steps.title: Complete the Application
steps.content: A SASSA officer will help you fill out the application form. You may be referred to a state doctor for a second medical assessment.

steps.title: Attend the State Medical Assessment
steps.content: If required, attend the assessment with a state doctor. This is usually scheduled within a few weeks of your application.

steps.title: Wait for the Outcome
steps.content: Processing takes between 30 and 90 days. You will receive an SMS notification of the outcome.

sections.title: Payment Amounts & Dates
sections.content: The Disability Grant amount is {{disability_grant_amount}} per month in 2026. Payments are made in the first week of each month, typically from the 4th to the 6th. If your grant is approved temporarily, you will need to reapply when it expires. A new medical assessment will be required to confirm that the disability persists.

faqs.q: Can I receive the Disability Grant and work part-time?
faqs.a: Yes, but your income must remain below the means test threshold. If you earn more than {{disability_income_threshold_single}} per month, your grant may be reduced or cancelled.

faqs.q: What happens if I turn 60 while receiving the Disability Grant?
faqs.a: Your Disability Grant will automatically convert to the Older Persons Grant. You do not need to reapply.
If your grant was awarded for a temporary period, you will need to be reassessed when it expires. If it improves permanently, you should inform SASSA.

faqs.q: Can I apply if I have a private doctor's report?
faqs.a: Yes, but SASSA may still require you to see a state doctor for confirmation. The final decision is based on the state assessment.
